title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 7 begins a systematic study of the boundary strata \hat M_G of the stable-curve moduli multiplicity \bar M_{g,\nu} that have dimension at most 2. G is an 'MD-graph' (Mumford–Deligne graph), i.e. the weighted dual graph of a stable marked curve. Each vertex \alpha carries a genus g_\alpha, a valence/order \omega_\alpha and a number \nu_\alpha of marked points (its 'weight'). The first step is to determine which MD-graphs occur.

Case I, dimension 0. The following conditions on G are stated to be equivalent:
(a) dim M_G = 0, equivalently dim \hat M_G = 0.
(b) The 'modular dimension' of G is 0. That is, the number s_1 of edges (the modular codimension of the stratum) reaches its maximum 3(g-1)+\nu.
(c) G is extremal for the generalisation order on MD-graphs: every generalisation morphism G' -> G is an isomorphism. In modern terms the stratum is a closed point, i.e. G is maximally degenerate.
(d) Every vertex has genus 0 and order \omega_\alpha \le 3, with \nu_\alpha = 3 - \omega_\alpha. Equivalently, every vertex has exactly 3 special points: a trivalent graph, or pants decomposition, with legs.

Consequence. Each component is P^1 with three distinguished points, which is rigid with no automorphisms. So over any base S there is, up to unique isomorphism, exactly one G-pinned ('G-épinglée') curve. This gives (60) M_G = \hat M_G \cong Spec Z =: S_0. The non-rigidified stratum is then the classifying multiplicity (stack) of the constant group Γ = Aut G over Spec Z: (61) M_{[G]} \cong B(Γ_{S_0}).

This serves the enumeration on the next page of strata of dimension \le 2. Those are the 'two first levels' of the Teichmüller tower that the Esquisse d'un programme singles out as generating everything.
errors: No real error on this page. One implicit point: for (61) to be correct, Aut G must be taken as automorphisms of the graph with half-edges. Then loops whose two branches are swapped contribute; with vertices and edges alone this would undercount.
The direction of the 'generalisation' order in (c) is left implicit. The meaning is that G is maximally degenerate, i.e. the stratum is a closed point.

On the next page, formula (63), as transcribed, writes 3(g-1)+\nu = 3(h_1(G)-1)+\nu. That only makes sense for the specific weighted conventions used (all vertex genera 0); it is not a general identity.

ideas.what: 0-dimensional boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n} correspond exactly to stable graphs with all vertices genus 0 and trivalent (counting legs); the number of edges is then maximal, 3g-3+n
ideas.modern_name: maximal degenerations / pants decompositions / trivalent stable graphs
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of the Teichmüller tower and pants decompositions

ideas.what: Rigidity: over Spec Z there is a unique G-pinned stable curve, so the rigidified stratum is Spec Z
ideas.modern_name: 0-dimensional strata are Spec Z; the stratum stack is the classifying stack BAut(G)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (e.g. stratification of \bar M_{g,n} by dual graphs; Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths vol. II)

ideas.what: Stratum of the moduli multiplicity attached to [G] is BΓ for Γ = Aut G, as a 'multiplicité classifiante' of a constant group over Spec Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in the theory of boundary strata (Graber–Pandharipande etc.)

ideas.what: Programme of enumerating all strata of modular dimension \le 2
ideas.modern_name: the 'two-level principle' for the Teichmüller tower
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); later Lochak, Schneps, Nakamura, Harbater–Schneps

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard characterisation of 0-dimensional boundary strata (trivalent genus-0 stable graphs, rigid over Spec Z, stack BAut G). Its interest is only as the working-out of the Esquisse's dimension \le 2 programme in Grothendieck's own 'multiplicité' language.
transcription_corrections: 'Conditions précisées sur le MD-graphe G sont équivalentes' should most likely read 'Les conditions suivantes sur le MD-graphe G sont équivalentes'.
'(60) M_G = M_{\hat G}' is more likely 'M_G = \hat M_G' (the hat is on M), consistent with condition (a).
In (d): 'et est d'ordre ω_α ≤ 3 ; le poids ν_α est égal à 3-ω_α'.
'[-Champ-] {+multiplicité classifiante+}' is confirmed: 'Champ' is struck and replaced by 'multiplicité classifiante de la relation en groupes'. Γ = Aut G with G underlined.
